title: Talent / Executive Search
markdown:
The **talent** module (`openexecutive.talent`) is a vertical built on top of Open Executive that turns the executive-advisor runtime into an executive-search platform. It is single-tenant and reuses the existing agent runtime, RAG, scheduler, workflow engine, and shared SQLite database rather than introducing new infrastructure.

This is **in-house hiring**: searches are run *within* this company, not on behalf of external clients.

## Entities

Three core records, persisted in the shared `episodic_memory.db` via `talent.store` (the same idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `_resolve_db_path` convention as `people.store`):

- **Engagement** — one search: a role we're hiring for in this company (`engagements`, status `open` / `on_hold` / `filled` / `cancelled`). Optional free-text `department` label (e.g. "Drilling") for in-house grouping — not a FK to the departments entity.
- **Candidate** — a person considered for an engagement (`candidates`, FK `engagement_id`) moving through the pipeline `lead → screened → interviewed → offer → placed`, with `rejected` as a terminal off-ramp. `fit_score` (0-100) and `screening_summary` are owned by `record_screening` (set by the `candidate_screen` workflow), never by the plain candidate-edit path.
- **Offer** — an offer to a candidate (`offers`, FKs `candidate_id` + `engagement_id`). Lifecycle is enforced by a transition map in `set_offer_status`: `draft → pending_approval → extended → accepted / declined / expired / rescinded` (rescind is also legal from draft/pending; pending may fall back to draft; terminals are immutable — re-offering means a new row). At most **one open offer per candidate**. `expires_at` is set at *extend* time, and expiry never auto-flips the status — only `record_offer_decision` does, on the principal's say-so. `package_md` carries the full offer-package artifact; `approval_run_id` / `approved_by_person_id` record the sign-off; `nudge_action_ids_json` tracks the scheduled expiry reminders so a decision can cancel them.

The original external-**Client** entity was removed; engagement is now top-level. Because there is no migration tooling, `initialize_db` does a one-time reset — it drops the legacy talent tables when it detects a `clients` table, then rebuilds the new shape. Recruiting workflows that named the hiring org now use *this* company's name (from the profile via `reminders.company_name()`).

## Talent specialist

`talent` — Head of Talent & Executive Search (`openexecutive.agents.talent`, deep-reasoning), registered in `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY`. Prompt `TALENT_PROMPT` in `prompts/domain_prompts.py`; the RAG alias maps `talent → ["hr", "strategy"]` until a dedicated talent corpus is seeded.

## Matching graph (Phase 2)

Non-archived candidates are indexed into a dedicated ChromaDB collection `talent_candidates` (kept separate from the knowledge/company collections so candidate profiles never blend into RAG). `talent.graph` exposes `match_candidates_for_engagement` (ranks the whole pool against a role's must-haves) and `find_similar_candidates` (excludes the query candidate). Indexing is best-effort — a vector-store outage degrades search but never breaks candidate CRUD.

## Recruiting workflows (Phase 3)

Four workflows, all **draft-and-approve** — they schedule reminders to the **principal** and never message candidates or references directly (candidates are not roster `Person` records). They share `talent.reminders` (`resolve_reminder_context`, `principal_channel`, `schedule_reminder`):

- **candidate_screen** — scores a candidate against an engagement; persists the fit score + scorecard.
- **candidate_outreach** — first-touch + timed follow-up reminders.
- **interview_coordination** — interview loop + availability request.
- **reference_check** — reference rubric + reference outreach.

Multi-LLM is intentionally not a separate build: non-Claude models already route via OpenRouter by model slug.

## Closing the hire loop

Two workflows take the funnel past "interviewed" — through the offer and into the first 90 days:

- **offer_approval** — drafts the offer package for an interviewed candidate (terms via the `chro` specialist anchored on the engagement's `comp_band`; closing plan — risks, competing-offer posture, recommended expiry window — via the `talent` specialist), persists the Offer (`pending_approval`, package on the row), advances the candidate to `offer`, DMs the **HIRING_SIGNOFF** approver (`find_approvers`, principal fallback), and pauses on a `WaitForHumanEvent` gate — the **first built-in workflow to use the gate**. Because paused runs never auto-resume (see [Workflows](#workflows)), the gate exists to *record* the sign-off: the `pending_approval → extended` transition is the explicit `extend_offer` follow-up (chat tool or `POST /offers/{id}/extend`), which consults the recorded resolution via `talent.offers` — a recorded rejection blocks it; a pending/absent sign-off proceeds on the principal's explicit instruction with the gap flagged in the response.
- **new_hire_onboarding** — the placed → `Person` handoff. Requires the candidate to be `placed` or hold an accepted offer. Idempotently creates/updates the roster Person (match by email, else exact name; role from the engagement; no authority scopes granted), drafts a role-specific 30/60/90 plan via the `chro` specialist, and schedules day-7/30/60/90 check-in reminders to the principal. Person creation is **never** an implicit side effect of a stage change — `record_offer_decision(accepted)` and `set_candidate_stage(placed)` only *suggest* running it.

Expiry posture: `extend_offer` schedules T−3d / T−1d / T+12h reminder nudges (plain `ad_hoc` scheduled actions assigned to the principal). Nudges remind; they never write. The candidate-contact invariant extends here: OE never sends an offer to a candidate and never messages a new hire — the approver gets the sign-off request, the principal gets the reminders.

## Chat & briefing integration

The vertical is wired into the three surfaces that make Open Executive feel like one assistant, so it is not a siloed UI:

- **MCP server** — the executive-search pipeline is exposed to *external* agents over the [MCP server](#mcp_server): an `oe://talent/engagements` resource plus read-only search tools (`list_candidates`, `get_candidate`, `match_candidates`, `find_similar_candidates`) that read `talent.store` and rank via `talent.graph`. The `talent` specialist's advice is reachable there via `consult_specialist`. Writes and workflow execution are deliberately not exposed over MCP.
- **Chat tools** (`orchestrator.talent_tools`, registered in the Executive's main loop) let the Executive act on the pipeline in conversation. Read tools — `list_engagements`, `list_candidates`, `get_candidate`, `match_candidates`, `list_offers` — never emit an action chip; the write tools are side-effecting and chipped: `set_candidate_stage` (a light, reversible pipeline move), `start_talent_workflow` (runs the talent workflows via the runs store; `offer_approval` pauses on its gate and reports `awaiting_human` instead of completing), `create_engagement` / `create_candidate` (build the pipeline from chat, mirroring the `/talent` API routes), and the offer-lifecycle tools `create_offer` (manual draft when the principal dictates terms), `extend_offer`, and `record_offer_decision` (`accepted` also places the candidate and fills the engagement). The shared extend/decide logic lives in `talent.offers` so chat and HTTP can't drift. The `/talent` UI remains the home for heavier editing and bulk work.
- **Briefing** — `briefing.talent_digest` rolls active engagements up by pipeline stage (`offers_expiring_soon` / `needs_screening` / `offers_out` / `stalled` signals — expiring offers are computed straight from `expires_at`, so a missed nudge can't make the briefing stale). This one rollup feeds the `/today` `talent` field, the briefing's **Executive search** card (click-to-discuss → chat), the 'what's going on' narrative, and the chat `<briefing>` block — so the cards, the header, and chat never disagree about a search's state.

## API & UI

`api.routes.talent` exposes CRUD for `/engagements`, `/candidates` (plus `/candidates/{id}/stage`, per-entity `/archive`), the graph endpoints `GET /engagements/{id}/matches`, `GET /candidates/{id}/similar`, `POST /talent/reindex`, and the offer lifecycle: `GET`/`POST /offers`, `GET`/`PATCH /offers/{id}`, `POST /offers/{id}/extend`, `POST /offers/{id}/decision`, `POST /offers/{id}/archive` (lifecycle conflicts are 409s). The `/talent` UI renders the pipeline board, the **Searches** list at `/talent/searches`, and candidate detail — which now carries an **Offer panel** (status pill, terms, collapsible package, expiry countdown, lifecycle buttons, and the onboarding launcher once the candidate is hired).

## Deferred

CRM/ATS integration, direct candidate sends ("Phase 3b"), automated resume intake, and multi-tenancy (Phase 4) are not yet built.
